- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.5) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in responding to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative after 3–5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise and avoid extreme swings.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 60% history, 40% sentiment) to calibrate forecast.
